messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find public libraries in New York with reading room and fiction section, in Los Angeles with Wi-Fi and children section, and in Chicago with cafe and reading room. We need to use the function public_library_find_nearby. We need to call it three times with appropriate parameters.

We need to provide the function calls. The function signature: public_library_find_nearby({location: string, facilities: ...}). The facilities parameter can be one of the listed options: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

But the facilities parameter expects a single value? It says "Facilities and sections in public library." It lists options separated by |. But also "Cafe"[] indicates array? The type is ambiguous. Possibly we need to pass an array of strings? The description: "Facilities and sections in public library." The options: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

It might mean that facilities can be one of those strings or an array of strings if multiple. The example shows "Cafe"[] meaning array of cafes? Actually "Cafe"[] means array of "Cafe"? That seems odd. Maybe they want to pass an array of strings like ["Cafe", "Reading Room"].

Thus for each location, we need to pass facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"] for NY; ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"] for LA; ["Cafe", "Reading Room"] for Chicago.

We need to call the function three times. Provide the calls.
